steps.title: Build the invariant rental walkthrough brief
steps.prompt_exact: Can you make a saveable offline browser scorecard I can use during an apartment walkthrough to rate each room, note hazards and lease-risk clues, attach photo notes, and copy a clean inspection brief at the end?
steps.response_exact:
All scans clean — zero hits on innerHTML, inline handlers, modal APIs, external deps, URL literals, letter-spacing, and vw/clamp font sizing, and the JS passes a syntax check.Single file, fully offline. How it works:

**Rooms** — starts with entry, living, kitchen, bath, and bedroom 1; add or remove any. Each room gets a big 1–5 tap score (1–2 render in hazard orange, 3–5 in green), 12 hazard chips (mold/moisture, fresh paint over stains, pest bait stations, missing smoke/CO detector, etc.), free notes, and photo attachments. Photos open your camera on mobile, get downscaled to 1024px JPEG so storage doesn't blow up, and each takes a caption.

**Lease-risk clues** — a global chip set for the softer red flags: listing mismatch, rushed showing, vague deposit terms, repairs promised verbally, utilities not separately metered, plus a notes box for landlord questions.

**Brief** — one tap builds a plain-text summary: average score, hazard and clue counts, room-by-room breakdown with photo captions, and an auto-generated "follow-ups before signing" list (every hazard becomes a "get remediation in writing" item, and flagged clues like verbal repair promises generate addendum requests). Copy uses the clipboard API with a select-and-copy fallback for file:// contexts.

**Persistence** — autosaves to localStorage (debounced, with a save indicator), plus JSON export/import so you can back up or move between phone and desktop. Destructive actions (remove room, clear all) use two-tap arm/confirm instead of modals. If photo storage hits the quota, the save indicator flips orange and tells you to trim photos or export.
steps.response_summary: Claude returned the first complete one-file apartment walkthrough scorecard.
steps.notes: Preserved exact first artifact. Functional and viewport checks passed, but static verification found document.execCommand.

steps.title: Remove the deprecated inspection-brief copy fallback
steps.prompt_exact: I tested the saved file and found one concrete safety issue: the clipboard fallback still calls document.execCommand, and our public artifact verifier rejects that deprecated token. Remove document.execCommand entirely; use navigator.clipboard when available and otherwise leave the generated brief visible, focused, and selected for manual copying. Keep the room scores, hazard and lease-risk flags, photo notes, local save/import/export, inspection brief, offline behavior, and current design unchanged, then return the complete updated self-contained HTML file.
steps.response_exact:
Fixed. `document.execCommand` is gone entirely — zero hits on the re-scan, along with clean passes on all the original checks and JS syntax.

New copy behavior: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` when available; otherwise (or if it rejects, which happens on some file:// contexts) the fallback focuses the brief textarea, selects the full text via `select()` + `setSelectionRange`, and shows "Brief selected — press Ctrl+C (or Cmd+C) to copy" in the status line. Also dropped the readonly-toggle dance since it only existed to support execCommand — the textarea stays readonly throughout, which doesn't block selection or manual copying. Everything else is untouched.
steps.response_summary: Claude removed document.execCommand and returned the complete corrected scorecard.
steps.continuation_reason: Verification-proven defect: the first artifact used document.execCommand in its inspection-brief copy fallback.

comparison_basis.opening_prompt_exact: Can you make a saveable offline browser scorecard I can use during an apartment walkthrough to rate each room, note hazards and lease-risk clues, attach photo notes, and copy a clean inspection brief at the end?
acceptance_criteria: Support room-by-room scoring with hazards, lease-risk clues, severity, and evidence or photo-note fields.
Keep the overall rental assessment synchronized with the current room findings.
Provide useful local save or restore behavior without uploading private inspection data.
Provide a clean copyable or downloadable inspection brief suitable for a real rental decision.
Produce one complete self-contained HTML file that is immediately usable in a browser.
Operate offline with no external APIs, hosted generation, CDNs, remote fonts, scripts, stylesheets, or fragile dependencies.
Avoid unsafe HTML sinks, eval-like execution, inline event handlers, modal dialogs, and deprecated clipboard handling.
Avoid page-level horizontal overflow at 390 by 844 and at desktop width.
Keep essential controls visible, keyboard or touch reachable, and truthful about their current state.
Preserve exact prompt, response, source, and artifact-version evidence for the run.
comparison_basis.adaptive_repair_policy: Preserve and score the first real artifact. Continue only when verification proves a concrete defect or a source-capture failure; use the same source session and model; name the observed defect in ordinary language; preserve every real artifact version; stop as soon as the artifact passes; prefer no more than three total prompts and go beyond three only for a documented concrete lane reason such as a verification-proven regression, truncation, or mechanical capture failure.
comparison_basis.independence_note: Claude received the invariant brief in a fresh session and was not shown the historical implementation, screenshots, source code, or another provider's output.
